C0.quote: Given a set of n rankings provided by voters on d candidates
C0.note: Fair rank aggregation (Kemeny-type) with approximation algorithms; borderline but treated as aggregation of voters' rankings into a collective ranking.

C1.quote: there exists a (2 + ε)-approximation algorithm for the fair rank aggregation problem
C1.note: Approximation algorithms are the main results; experiments on real-world datasets are secondary.

C2.1.quote: minimizes the sum of distances to the input rankings

C2.2.quote: We refer to the set of all rankings (or permutations) over [d]

C2.3.quote: multiple voters provide preference orders or rankings on candidates
C2.3.note: Mentions preference orders and the preference order of a single voter; weakly present.

C2.4.quote: it is essentially influenced by the preference order of a single voter
C2.4.note: Rankings are treated as preferences and the rule is applied directly, with no statement about submission or reporting.

C3.2.note: No statement that voters submit held attitudes.

C4.1.note: No utility, welfare or satisfaction for voters used.

C5.1.note: The objective is the sum of Kendall tau distances, and fairness is for candidate groups. This is not voter welfare, representation of voters or distortion.

VOT.note: Voters only supply fixed input rankings and take no action in the model.

C8.1.note: No strategic agents, so C8 does not apply.

claims.quote: it is essential for any ranking algorithm to produce a fair ranking
it is essentially influenced by the preference order of a single voter

C9.1.note: The claims concern real decisions such as hiring and admissions, and fairness to candidate groups.

C9.2.quote: to ensure equitable selection and to avoid the risk of reinforcing
C9.2.note: Claims about real applications need an unstated link between input rankings and held preferences, and that the Kendall tau objective and group quotas capture fairness.
